description: Accumulated undocumented items from previous crews had unknown provenance and no disposal record. Crew 16's Commander described surprise at the number of items and the effort required to sort them.
response: Crew 16 spent significant rainy-day time cataloguing the items and began a formal electronic inventory.
lesson: Request Crew 16's electronic inventory from the Mars Society before departure. Every crew must make a leave/discard/return decision for every item at mission close and document it.
source_citation: SRC-hypatia-iii-brief, Part IV – Incident and emergency register, §4.3 Operational incidents, lines 668-673. Register Crew tag: 'All (register tag; content specifically discusses Crew 16's Commander)'. Sol: not stated; 'rainy-day time' cataloguing placed at a representative early-to-mid mission rainy day. Confidence (C) rationale: register tags this entry 'All' but names the Commander specifically; assigned to FMARS-C16-2024; Commander-narrative account, XO/Commander-report style. Reclassification note (2026-08-26): originally classified Failure; on review, the substantive content here is Crew 16 introducing a new process (a formal electronic inventory) in response to an inherited documentation gap, not a system or process failing during their own mission. Reclassified to Process Innovation; outcome (Partially Resolved) kept as-is since the inventory was only begun, not completed, during the mission.
